actual.nearest_data: City government searches did not retrieve an in-boundary groundwater concentration. MPWMD 2023–2024 Mitigation Program Report, section IV-B, printed pp.IV-2–IV-4 (PDF pp.43–45), monitors the Carmel Valley alluvial aquifer and coastal Seaside Basin; five lower-Carmel-Valley wells were sampled in November 2024, and its published summary emphasizes conductivity/chloride. These networks are not the incorporated city (https://www.mpwmd.net/wp-content/uploads/MPWMD-MitigationReport-finalRY2024.pdf). For the accepted county fallback, Current local-government monitoring was examined before state sources. Monterey Subbasin WY2025 report, section 4.4.3.2 (printed p.87 / PDF p.95), reports selected coastal-well nitrate results from non-detect to approximately 6 mg/L as N, including approximately 5 mg/L in MCWD-30; these are selected wells, not a county statistic (https://www.mcwd.org/docs/gsa/3-004.10_WY_2025.pdf). The Water Board 2025 agricultural memo Figure 2 has 2024 NO3-N distributions and sample counts by subbasin, including East Side, Forebay, Upper Valley and 180/400 Foot; these on-farm domestic wells do not cover all county groundwater (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/water_issues/programs/ilp/docs/2025/gw-quality-tech-memo.pdf). The 2024 GAP report Tables 2–3 reports 253 Monterey wells tested and 141 nitrate-MCL exceedances over October 2018–July 2024; this voluntary cumulative sample is neither a recent concentration nor representative county coverage (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/board_info/agendas/2024/dec/item12_stfrpt.pdf). The 2024 Aquifer Risk Map layer uses depth-filtered/de-clustered well data but exposes a 20-year comparison-concentration index, recent exceedance counts and risk classes, not a recent county concentration (https://gispublic.waterboards.ca.gov/portalserver/rest/services/Hosted/Water_Quality_Risk_2024_ARM/FeatureServer/5).
